generationContext.text:
# Microsoft Azure Batch management client library for .NET

Use Microsoft Azure Batch to run large-scale parallel and high-performance computing (HPC) batch jobs efficiently in Azure. Azure Batch creates and manages a pool of compute nodes (virtual machines), installs the applications you want to run, and schedules jobs to run on the nodes. 

This library supports managing Microsoft Azure Batch resources.

This library follows the [new Azure SDK guidelines](https://azure.github.io/azure-sdk/general_introduction.html), and provides many core capabilities:

    - Support MSAL.NET, Azure.Identity is out of box for supporting MSAL.NET.
    - Support [OpenTelemetry](https://opentelemetry.io/) for distributed tracing.
    - HTTP pipeline with custom policies.
    - Better error-handling.
    - Support uniform telemetry across all languages.

## Getting started 

### Install the package

Install the Microsoft Azure Batch management library for .NET with [NuGet](https://www.nuget.org/):

```dotnetcli
dotnet add package Azure.ResourceManager.Batch
```

### Prerequisites

* You must have an [Microsoft Azure subscription](https://azure.microsoft.com/free/dotnet/).

### Authenticate the Client

To create an authenticated client and start interacting with Microsoft Azure resources, see the [quickstart guide here](https://github.com/Azure/azure-sdk-for-net/blob/main/doc/dev/mgmt_quickstart.md).

## Key concepts

Key concepts of the Microsoft Azure SDK for .NET can be found [here](https://azure.github.io/azure-sdk/dotnet_introduction.html).

## Documentation

Documentation is available to help you learn how to use this package:

- [Quickstart](https://github.com/Azure/azure-sdk-for-net/blob/main/doc/dev/mgmt_quickstart.md).
- [API References](https://learn.microsoft.com/dotnet/api/?view=azure-dotnet).
- [Authentication](https://github.com/Azure/azure-sdk-for-net/blob/main/sdk/identity/Azure.Identity/README.md).

## Examples

Code samples for using the management library for .NET can be found in the following locations
- [.NET Management Library Code Samples](https://aka.ms/azuresdk-net-mgmt-samples)

## Troubleshooting

-   File an issue via [GitHub Issues](https://github.com/Azure/azure-sdk-for-net/issues).
-   Check [previous questions](https://stackoverflow.com/questions/tagged/azure+.net) or ask new ones on Stack Overflow using Azure and .NET tags.

## Next steps

For more information about Microsoft Azure SDK, see [this website](https://azure.github.io/azure-sdk/).

## Contributing

For details on contributing to this repository, see the [contributing
guide][cg].

This project welcomes contributions and suggestions. Most contributions
require you to agree to a Contributor License Agreement (CLA) declaring
that you have the right to, and actually do, grant us the rights to use
your contribution. For details, visit <https://cla.microsoft.com>.

When you submit a pull request, a CLA-bot will automatically determine
whether you need to provide a CLA and decorate the PR appropriately
(for example, label, comment). Follow the instructions provided by the
bot. You'll only need to do this action once across all repositories
using our CLA.

This project has adopted the [Microsoft Open Source Code of Conduct][coc]. For
more information, see the [Code of Conduct FAQ][coc_faq] or contact
<opencode@microsoft.com> with any other questions or comments.

decisions.reason: Both source-defined pool factory overloads call another overload with taskSchedulingPolicy set to null; the first extracts VmConfiguration and the second forwards tags and upgradePolicy. The listed parameters not forwarded are visible in their signatures and call sites. This is a model factory API-shape preservation rather than an independently implemented poller; retaining earlier signatures is not a generally generator-addressable change.

Lines 141–146 explicitly mark the factory method obsolete and hidden, and its body returns a parameterless certificate data object without using the inputs. Its compatibility-stub pattern and no addressability judgment fit the source.

Lines 149–154 show an obsolete, hidden certificate-content factory whose body ignores its inputs and returns a parameterless object. The cited model-factory stub supports the proposed classification and compatibility judgment.

Lines 157–162 define a source-level model factory with a null-tags default and a nested DetectorResponseProperties object containing value. A general model-factory method could plausibly provide this flattened mocking API.

Lines 165–170 define the application output factory and explicitly group its three named inputs in an ApplicationProperties object after defaulting tags. This is a model factory API shape that could plausibly be generated.

Lines 173–178 show the output factory defaulting tags and passing state, format, URI and timestamps into ApplicationPackageProperties. The finding identifies this distinct model factory overload with bounded evidence.

Lines 181–188 show defaulting tags and groupIds, conditionally constructing PrivateEndpoint, materializing groupIds and constructing the nested properties. The citation and model-factory classification fit this source-defined overload.

Lines 191–198 show a separate private-link output factory defaulting tags and both sequences, converting them to lists and constructing nested properties. Its model-factory pattern and plausible generator addressability are supported.

The collection is not a model override: its retained operations and enumerable interfaces throw NotSupportedException. Classify the retired collection API surface as Other, retaining the exact original path and symbols.

decisions.reason: Lines 20–61 retain an obsolete data type and its fields, with a constructor initializing Tags; lines 74–85 show unsupported read/write implementations except the J format selection. This is source-level retention of a model API, not an operational serializer.

Lines 66–72 explicitly declare an obsolete Thumbprint alias and its null-aware BinaryData conversion to and from ThumbprintString. Keeping this older property is a separate model API compatibility behavior.

This retained resource class is not a model override: the visible operations are unsupported stubs, while ResourceType and CreateResourceIdentifier still supply metadata and an ID builder. Reclassify its compatibility surface as Other and distinguish the working ID builder from the throwing methods.

limitations: Coverage is partial: four files were captured from 420 eligible files and 458 discovered files; 23 additional paths are explicitly budget-skipped. Findings describe only the supplied bounded source.
The generated overloads called by the pool factories and the definitions of nested property models were not supplied; only the forwarding expressions and construction visible here are assessed.
Obsolete certificate APIs are retained as declarations or throwing stubs. Their presence does not demonstrate working certificate service operations, pagination or LRO polling.
Package metadata and generation context establish scope but do not establish additional behavior or a measured cause for these implementations.
Only four of 420 eligible files are captured; skipped source cannot be assessed and these decisions do not imply package-wide completeness.

Generated counterparts and earlier released APIs are not supplied, so compatibility intent and exact differences from generated signatures cannot be independently confirmed beyond the cited source annotations and calls.

The retained certificate resource combines working identifier construction with unsupported operation and serialization stubs; these are described separately within the cited API-retention finding rather than asserting operational resource behavior.
